critical_code_review_comments: ReportsPage.js:55 fetchReport(type, tab, overrideFilters) — correctly uses overrideFilters to bypass stale-closure via `const f = overrideFilters ? { ...filters, ...overrideFilters } : filters;`. Pattern is sound. Consider renaming to fetchReportWithFilters for clarity, and extracting the similar inline pattern for other filters that may suffer the same bug in future.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Both iteration_21 action items are resolved and verified. The ReportsPage.js Movement filter now responds on first click and the backend movement summary reflects unfiltered totals. For any future movement-related work, the canonical pytest regression is /app/backend/tests/test_iteration22_retest.py (covers cross-filter consistency). The iteration_21 test file has one brittle strict-equality assertion (usage_count == 5) that fails after re-runs due to non-cleaned usage_logs — this is a test-hygiene issue, not a product bug. BASE_URL must be exported from frontend/.env before running pytest: `export $(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL frontend/.env) && pytest ...`.
rca of the issue: Both fixes validated. BUG 1 root cause was stale closure: setFilters followed by fetchReport in the same tick captured the previous filters. Fix applied by E1: fetchReport now accepts overrideFilters and the Select onValueChange at ReportsPage.js:143 passes { movement_type: v } so the fresh value is merged BEFORE the request is built. BUG 2 root cause was counter computation order: fast_count/slow_count were being computed AFTER `movement_rows = [r for r in movement_rows if r['movement_type'].lower()==mt_norm]`, so filtering to 'slow' zeroed out fast_count. Fix applied by E1: counters are now computed at server.py:2627-2628 BEFORE the filter application at line 2631.
